source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Somerset, NJ campus, NYM1, publishes 23 MW of IT capacity and 185,000 square feet of technical space, the second largest published figure in New Jersey.

The 23 MW is the only firm number here. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, that load is roughly 575 racks, but that is an assumption about density rather than a claim by CyrusOne. At a lower density the same 23 MW means more racks and fewer accelerators per rack, so the accelerator count depends entirely on a density the operator does not publish. The 185,000 square feet of technical space is the building constraint that sits alongside the power constraint, and neither figure tells you how the two are used together.

New Jersey has 48 mapped facilities, but only 5 publish a megawatt figure, and those 5 total 111.3 MW. This campus alone is 23 MW of that 111.3 MW, about a fifth of all published capacity in the state. The other 43 mapped facilities publish nothing, so the state's real total is unknown and almost certainly larger than 111.3 MW. Published capacity in New Jersey is a floor, not a census.

What the data does not cover matters as much as what it does. No certifications are published, so nothing here qualifies the campus for a specific class of tenant. No address or postal code is given. No announced expansion is recorded, which is the one input the suitability score is missing. The score of 64 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type, so it measures what CyrusOne discloses, not what the site can ultimately deliver.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
